title: Chapter 41
content:
When Jakyeong finally blinked his eyes open, the bedroom was plunged in twilight as if it were the dead of night.

He reached toward the bedside table, but his fingers met empty air—no smartphone, no wristwatch. He pushed himself upright to flick on the lamp, nearly letting out a strangled shriek as a wave of brutal agony tore through every joint in his body. It felt like he’d been beaten with lead pipes.

Checking the digital wall clock, it was well past noon.

Dragging his stiff limbs off the mattress, he walked over to the floor-to-ceiling windows and parted the heavy blackout blinds. Blinding, high-noon sunlight flooded the room, stinging his eyes so fiercely he had to shield his face with a forearm before shuffling toward the master bathroom.

The reflection staring back from the vanity mirror made him freeze in morbid horror.

A literal zombie was standing in the frame. His lips were swollen and bruised, hollow dark rings hung beneath his bloodshot eyes, and his throat was painted in a violent patchwork of mottled purples and reds.

He yanked his shirt up over his chest and ribs—the blooming bruises looked less like love bites and more like a terminal infectious outbreak.

"Fucking lunatic..."

Jakyeong squeezed his eyes shut, the relentless sensory memory of what Kang Il-hyun had done to him flooding back. Breached, driven into, and filled again and again—he had lost count of how many times the man had taken him to the brink and emptied himself inside. Jakyeong had always prided himself on his elite physical stamina, but he had blacked out halfway through the marathon from sheer sensory overload.

The original mark left by Choi Ki-tae had been sucked so savagely by Il-hyun that the skin had darkened to a deep, swollen plum, spreading over twice the surface area.

Needing something to clear the mental fog, Jakyeong fished out his cigarettes. Sitting on the marble lip of the tub with a hollow, shell-shocked stare, he torched two cigarettes down to the filter in rapid succession.

Shuffling back to the basin, he squeezed a dollop of paste onto his toothbrush. His arms ached so intensely that even scrubbing his teeth felt like lifting dead weight. Having ground his teeth together all night to stifle his screams, his gums were swollen and bleeding into the white foam.

"Unbelievable."

Letting out a dry, incredulous scoff, he rinsed his mouth, stripped down, and stepped beneath the scalding shower spray. The damage wasn't limited to his chest and back—deep crimson marks blossomed down his flanks, inner thighs, and calves like a gruesome field of wild poppies. Leaving the estate looking like this was out of the question for the foreseeable future.

After drying off, he threw on the most concealing lounge clothes he could find and plastered several large pain-relief patches across his bruised neck.

His stomach growled with fierce urgency. Descending the grand staircase, the villa was dead silent—a small mercy, given that with every downward step, a sharp, throbbing ache radiated from his tailbone straight up his spine.

Stepping into the kitchen, the senior housekeeper turned around from the prep counter. Wiping her hands on her linen apron, she hurried over with a look of deep concern.

"I heard you were feeling under the weather, Young Master. I brewed a fresh pot of vegetable porridge—would you like a bowl now?"

Jakyeong shook his head firmly. "I need meat..."

He had lost an obscene amount of protein last night—or rather, had it systematically wrung out of him. Given how roughly his shaft had been handled, he half-wondered if Kang Il-hyun’s latent fingerprints were permanently bruised into the skin.

While the housekeeper began searing seasoned beef cuts on the range, Jakyeong collapsed across the living room sectional like a marionette with its strings cut.

Through the glass, the head gardener was methodically manicuring the sprawling lawn. The pristine summer weather made the emerald grass look blindingly vibrant.

Jakyeong retrieved his phone and pulled up the morning news feeds. Predictably, not a single publication carried a whisper about the bloodbath aboard the yacht last night. High-society crime was always neatly sanitized before it ever reached the press.

Resting his head against the cushions, the front door chime echoed through the foyer.

Jakyeong snapped upright, his guard flaring. If it was Kang Il-hyun, he was prepared to bolt straight back upstairs.

The figure rounding the corner was Kang Seok-joo.

"Hey, Yi-an! Just rolling out of bed?"

Seok-joo brandished an upscale boutique shopping bag with a wide grin.

"What's that?"

"Brought a vintage bottle of champagne for us to crack open by the pool."

Bringing champagne for a guy who doesn't drink alcohol and refuses to swim. The transparent excuse was almost funny.

"Haven't had lunch yet, right?"

"No... just woke up."

"Perfect. Let's eat poolside while taking a dip. Ma'am! Please send lunch out to the deck!"

Seok-joo scooped up his champagne bag and urged him outside.

Jakyeong’s plan of quietly nursing his broken body in bed all afternoon dissolved into thin air. Now that my cover is blown anyway, maybe I should just tell Kang Il-hyun to ban this brat from the house. Babysitting a spoiled heir was exhausting work.

Stepping out onto the stone patio, the midday heat struck like a furnace. Even sitting in the shade of the crimson umbrella, a light sweat beaded across Jakyeong's brow.

Seok-joo stripped down without ceremony, revealing a pair of neon-blue swim briefs. The kid was in decent shape, and his package was prominent enough, but compared to the monstrous proportions of Kang Il-hyun, it fell noticeably short.

Jakyeong blinked, inwardly horrified with himself. Why the hell am I mentally comparing the cock sizes of grown men?

Watching Seok-joo paddle lazily through the cobalt water without a care in the world, Jakyeong felt a sharp pang of envy. Some people really were born into pure, unearned luxury.

Moments later, a server brought out a silver platter alongside an ice bucket for the champagne. Each place setting was laid out with a thick, seared steak cut into bite-sized cubes, accompanied by roasted baby potatoes, grilled asparagus, and sweet caramelized onions, flanked by two tall glasses of fresh lemonade garnished with mint.

Hoisting himself onto the coping, Seok-joo immediately began flirting with the server, asking if she was free later that afternoon. The maid offered an ambiguous, practiced smile and retreated inside before things got awkward. Keep pushing your luck like that, and your brother will cave your skull in, Jakyeong thought dryly.

Popping the champagne cork, Seok-joo filled his flute. "Cheers."

Their crystal glasses tapped together, though Jakyeong stuck strictly to his mint lemonade.

Seok-joo’s eyes inevitably locked onto the thick layer of medicated patches plastered across Jakyeong’s throat. He asked what happened, and unable to confess the depraved truth, Jakyeong muttered an excuse about waking up with severe muscle spasms.

Midway through the meal, Seok-joo's phone buzzed violently.

Scanning the screen, his eyes widened with theatrical glee as he breathed out, "Holy shit..."

Without waiting to be asked, he leaned across the table, eager to spill the tea from his private group chats.

"Word on the street is Choi Ki-tae’s old man is dead."

Jakyeong blinked slowly, putting on a blank, uncomprehending mask. "Who?"

"Ki-tae’s father! The drug lord!"

"Ah..."

"Fucking wild, right? Group chats are blowing up. Ki-tae’s camp is frantically denying it, but the rumor is already spreading like wildfire through the circle."

Seok-joo looked like a tabloid journalist who’d just landed the scoop of the century. In this echelon of society, a gruesome death wasn't an occasion for mourning—it was cheap entertainment. Ignoring his lunch, Seok-joo began reading the group chat updates aloud like a live broadcast: from unverified leaks that the boss was butchered in his sleep, to credible eyewitness accounts claiming an armed disturbance had broken out at the yacht party before the patriarch vanished completely.

Jakyeong chewed his steak in absolute silence.

Unable to contain his curiosity, Seok-joo dialed Ki-tae's private number. When the line went straight to voicemail after three attempts, he tossed the phone onto the glass table with a disappointed pout.

"Straight to voicemail. Guess it's real."

"If he were actually dead, wouldn't there be a funeral?"

"I had a massive stake invested in their logistics line... Did I just throw that money away?"

"How much did you put in?"

Seok-joo held up all ten fingers without hesitation. It certainly wasn't ten million won. Nor was it a hundred million. Ten billion won?

"It's chump change in the grand scheme, but it was my very first independent venture."

"Invest in legitimate businesses..." Jakyeong sighed, taking a sip of lemonade. "Why trust criminals with that kind of capital?"

"Shows how little you know. Their return on investment blew everyone else out of the water. Besides, if Ki-tae’s family goes under, even Executive Director Kang takes a hit."

According to Seok-joo's insider rambling, few fixers in the country laundered offshore black money as cleanly as the late Choi Moon-sung, which meant Kang Il-hyun had utilized their channels on occasion. Furthermore, the private galas hosted by the Choi syndicate were elite networking hubs frequented by political heavyweights and judges, making them prime real estate for building leverage.

Jakyeong said nothing, quietly polishing off the rest of his steak.

While he satisfied his hollow stomach, Seok-joo continued trading rapid-fire conspiracy theories with his friends. Tapping out a text, Seok-joo looked up, a conspiratorial glint in his eye.

"Remember that incident where their street mules got hijacked from the precinct? I told you about that, right?"

"Yeah."

"Then Ki-tae’s younger brother gets executed, and now his father gets wiped out."

"And?"

"It's definitely the work of a single operator."

Look at that. The kid isn't completely braindead after all.

"You really think so...?"

"I'd bet my trust fund on it. Someone with a blood debt is methodically slaughtering the Choi bloodline. Ki-tae is probably next on the chopping block."

Seok-joo pushed up an imaginary pair of spectacles like a smug anime detective.

Jakyeong let out a quiet chuckle. "Watch your mouth... Guys who run around gossiping like that are usually the first ones to catch a stray bullet."

Seok-joo scoffed in arrogant dismissal. "You think someone could take me out that easily?"

Puffing his chest out, he raised his hands, mimicking holding a tactical rifle again. Watching him brace the imaginary buttstock directly against the bridge of his nose instead of his shoulder made Jakyeong let out a heavy, exasperated sigh. Fire a real rifle like that, and the recoil will shatter your nasal bone into your skull.

Jakyeong made a mental note: if an operational window opened before he left the country, he’d give this useless brat a proper crash course in firearms handling. At least that way, if the kid ever tried to square up against Kang Il-hyun, he’d go down putting up a fight.

As he watched with mild pity, Seok-joo suddenly flinched, snapping his arms down and scrambling to sit up straight.

Jakyeong didn't need to look over his shoulder to know who had just arrived.

He calmly dipped a piece of beef into the wholegrain mustard and popped it into his mouth. The frantic clicking of Seok-joo’s internal gears was practically audible, alongside the measured crunch of dress shoes against the manicured turf.

"What are you doing here?"

Il-hyun’s voice was arctic.

Seok-joo scrambled to his feet in an awkward, half-bent bow, while Il-hyun came to a halt directly beside Jakyeong’s chair. Jakyeong felt the man's dark gaze bore into the heavy patches plastered over his throat, but kept his eyes fixed forward.

"Brother... you told me the other day to drop by and keep Yi-an company..."

"Your presence isn't required. Get lost."

The abrupt dismissal left Seok-joo’s face flashing with brief, wounded indignation. Begs me to keep his guest entertained, and now treats me like a stray dog. Not daring to push his luck, the kid offered a hasty bow, scooped up his clothes, and scurried toward the villa.

Jakyeong watched the young man's drooping shoulders with a faint smirk, chewing through the remainder of his lunch.

Once the courtyard was clear, Kang Il-hyun walked around the glass table and took the seat directly across from him.

"Up already? You must have been exhausted."

The sheer, shameless audacity of the man playing the innocent gentleman was almost breathtaking.

Jakyeong narrowed his eyes in a cold glare, chewing the tender beef between his molars as if he were grinding Kang Il-hyun's flesh straight to bone.
